intro: The succession of royal capitals this region is built around — read it top to bottom.

entries.title: Ishanapura
entries.description: Capital of Chenla under Isanavarman I, and the first place Khmer temple architecture settled into a form of its own.

entries.title: Mahendraparvata
entries.titleKm: មហេន្ទ្របវ៌ត
entries.description: The mountain city where Jayavarman II declared himself universal monarch in 802, the act that begins the Angkorian era.

entries.title: Hariharalaya
entries.description: The plain below the mountain, where Indravarman I built the first state temple and the first great reservoir.

entries.title: Yasodharapura
entries.description: Five centuries of capital on one site — Angkor Wat, Angkor Thom, and the largest pre-industrial city in the world.

entries.title: Lingapura
entries.description: Jayavarman IV moved the court a hundred kilometres north-east and raised a seven-tier pyramid. It lasted sixteen years.

entries.title: Longvek
entries.description: The walled river capital of Ang Chan I, at the centre of Cambodia's maritime trade with China and the Malay world.

entries.title: Oudong
entries.description: Two and a half centuries of capital on a low ridge, crowned by the stupas of the kings buried there.

entries.title: Chaktomuk
entries.description: The capital returns to the four-rivers junction it first held in 1434. Norodom I builds the Royal Palace here in 1866.
